name: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16
description: A compact console co-developed by NEC and Hudson Soft, with an 8-bit CPU paired with 16-bit graphics hardware. It briefly outsold the Famicom in Japan, was sold in North America as the TurboGrafx-16, and became famous for shooters and arcade ports on credit-card-sized HuCards.
curiosities: HuCards are about the size of a credit card, and the Japanese PC Engine itself is only around 14 cm square.
The American TurboChips have their pin order reversed relative to Japanese HuCards, which acts as a crude region lock.
NEC's CD-ROM² add-on of 1988 was the first CD-ROM drive for a home video game console.
The HuC6280 is a modified 65C02 that includes the sound generator and a timer on the same die.
